Same cluster as ch01 par. 'Israel are truly good': Shabbos 89b with BR 2:4 (ruach of Mashiach; teshuvah likened to water) and Tikkunim 36 (water = Torah), both Torah and teshuvah rooted in maamar Bereishis against Keter.
Same chain: re'ach begadav = bogdav (Sanh. 37a), 'field which God blessed' = field of apples (Taanit 29b), and the Friday-night meal of Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin, with Shabbos 89b.
Teshuvah from love; Israel's heart is truly to Heaven (bogdav, rose among thorns, 'ka-sheleg yalbinu'); develops 'Israel are truly good' but without Shabbat/Eishes Chayil.
Friday-night meal of Chakal Tapuchin = 're'ach sadeh asher berakho', Taanit 29b, 'melech le-sadeh ne'evad', and Zohar I 129a on baalei teshuvah: the same field/teshuvah/Shabbat cluster.

The same exposition of 'lo tira le-veitah mi-sheleg': snow = Amalek's coldness that strikes even the great, Yaabetz (Temurah 16a), three fires, and Shabbos 89b. Already a footnote parallel (n. 49, 51, 62, 64).
Amalek as reishis goyim casting weariness and removing yirah; 'u-levavo yavin va-shav' as Binah/teshuvah. Shares the Amalek-coldness idea, not the Sarah/Shabbat structure.
'Asher karcha' = cooling the warmth of the Jewish heart, the beginning of all decline; Knesset Yisrael as 'ishah yiras Hashem'. Same Amalek idea, different frame (zechiras Amalek).
Milah given to an infant without his effort testifies 've-amech kulam tzaddikim', against Amalek; parallels the milah half of 'shanim = Shabbat and milah'.
Isaac the first circumcised at eight, Shabbat, and Amalek 'asher karcha' cooling Israel from Torah as the root of the yetzer: the same pairing of milah/Shabbat against Amalek's coldness.

candidates.why: Commentary on the very Zohar (I 128b-129a) Rav Tzadok quotes: Machpelah/Jerusalem 'bound above and bound below, therefore doubled'; reads the doubling as Malchut receiving and giving, not as the upper and lower Heh.

Explains the same Zohar: the field, not the cave, is 'doubled'; Jerusalem above and below aligned and bound to each other. Mostly about Adam and Eve's burial, so shares only the Jerusalem-doubling step.
Sarah merited Machpelah ('zamemah sadeh vatikachehu') by a life of cleaving to her root; Machpelah is the Heh of the Name, upper and lower Heh: the same reading as Rav Tzadok's.

Asks Rav Tzadok's exact question (Sarah never knew of Machpelah; why is it credited to her?) and answers with the Zohar's two Hehs, upper and lower worlds; Sarah 'lifted' the field (11:8) and Shabbat is the model (11:9).
Only a Hebrew paraphrase of R. Elazar's question (the field, not the cave, is called Machpelah); no development of the idea.

found.why: 'Zamemah sadeh' = Sarah's lifelong thought to join the lower to the upper, the 'field which God has blessed' raised to the upper world; 've-natlah' = lifting. Machpelah is the place of that joining.

Machpelah per the Zohar is the joining of the two Hehs (Binah, hidden world; Malchut, revealed world); Abraham understood it came by Sarah's merit, so she is 'the one who took it' though already dead: Rav Tzadok's answer.
'Zamemah sadeh' read as Sarah's lifelong aim, brought from potential to act after death; Machpelah rises into holiness, and Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come.
Rav Bruna's joining redemption to prayer is the yichud required of the complete worshipper, so his joy lasted all day: a Kabbalistic reading of the same Gemara (Rav Tzadok: revelation of Atika).

footnotes.text: **Sefat Emet, Chayei Sara 26** (Chassidus) — Sarah merited Machpelah ('zamemah sadeh') by a life spent cleaving to her root above; Machpelah is the Heh of the Name, the upper and lower Heh. This is Rav Tzadok's reading of the Zohar's 'doubled Heh.' ובאמת איתא דמערת המכפלה היא בחי' אות ה' שבשם ויש בה מילוי ה' ויש ה' עילאה ותתאה

**Shem MiShmuel, Chayei Sara 11:2, 11:6-9** (Chassidus) — It asks the same question: Sarah never knew of Machpelah, so why is it credited to her? It answers that Machpelah joins the upper and lower worlds (the two Hehs), and Sarah 'lifted' the field toward the upper one; Shabbat is the model of this joining. ועוד שלא מצינו בשום מקום ששרה ידעה מקודם ממערת המכפלה ובזוה"ק דאברהם הוה ידע לה, ולמה מייחס זה לשרה

**Shem MiShmuel, Chayei Sara 2:10** (Chassidus) — Also explains 'zamemah sadeh' of Machpelah, the doubled Heh, as Sarah's quality of separating from this world. From this it explains the custom of saying Eishes Chayil on Friday night, when one leaves this world's concerns and receives the neshamah yeseirah. ולפי הדברים הנ"ל יש סמך למנהגנו שאנו אומרים אשת חיל בלילי שבת

**Shem MiShmuel, Chayei Sara 5:7** (Chassidus) — 'Zamemah sadeh': all Sarah's thought was to join the lower world, 'the field which God has blessed,' to the upper; 'natlah' means she raised it. This is close to Rav Tzadok's lower-Shechinah 'field' and Sarah becoming Knesset Yisrael. והיינו שהיא היתה מגבהת שדה אשר ברכו ה' עלמא תתאה לעלמא עלאה

**Shem MiShmuel, Chayei Sara 6:4** (Chassidus) — Machpelah, per the Zohar, is the joining of the two Hehs, and Abraham knew he won it by Sarah's merit, so she is called the one who 'took' it though she had died. It gives Rav Tzadok's answer to the same question. ואברהם הבין דכל מה שזכה למערת המכפלה הכל הי' בזכות שרה, וע"כ נקרא על שמה שהיא היתה הלוקחת אף שבעת הלקיחה כבר מתה

**Sefat Emet, Chayei Sara 30:6** (Chassidus) — 'Zamemah sadeh' means that all Sarah's life aimed at preparing her place, and it came from potential to act after her death; Shabbat is likewise a foretaste of the World to Come. It answers the same difficulty in a different way. ובמדרש תנחומא איתא על שרה זממה שדה ותקחהו על מערת המכפלה. לומר שכל ימי חייה הי' כל מגמתה להכין לעצמה מקום בקבר

**Mikdash Melekh on Zohar I 128b–129a** (Kabbalah) — On the Zohar Rav Tzadok quotes: Jerusalem above and below are each 'bound on two sides,' receiving from above and giving below, and so it is called 'doubled.' He reads it as Malchut rather than as the two Hehs. נמצא שהיא אחידא לעילא ואחידא לתתא לכך נקראת מכפלה

**Ketem Paz on Zohar I 128b–129a** (Kabbalah) — It explains why the field, not the cave, is 'doubled': Jerusalem above and Jerusalem below are aligned and pour into each other. This is the Jerusalem step Rav Tzadok cites alongside Tanchuma Pekudei. ירושלם לעילא ירושלם לתתא אחידא לעילא ואחידא לתתא מכוונות זו כנגד זו ומשפעות זו לזו

**Avodat HaKodesh 2:44** (Kabbalah) — R. Meir ibn Gabbai reads Rav Bruna's joining of redemption to prayer as the yichud asked of the complete worshipper, so his joy lasted the whole day. Rav Tzadok reads the same joining as a revelation of Atika. הנה כי רב ברונא סמך גאולה לתפלה והוא הייחוד הנדרש מהעובד השלם
